Editor Flow

The editor allows you to build custom campaigns and to share them for others to play.

The editor involves 4 important concepts you must understand.  Patterns, Areas, Campaigns and Groups.  They each embed into each other and offers a modular system that makes patterns and areas reusable for everyone.

As a creator, you can make patterns and areas for you and other people to use as well build your own campaigns.
Patterns

The building blocks of Road of the Dead 2 are called Patterns. A pattern is a short section of road (90 meters/5 road strips long) that can contains obstacles, building, various road types, zombies, soldiers, trees, etc.  When you make one, you can save it, privately or publicly to use in your areas and to let other people use it in their own areas.
Areas

At a higher level than the patterns, you have areas.  An area is a group of patterns bound together.  For exemple, a forest area would contain many forest related patterns, one with just trees, one with a table and some garbage bins, a pattern with a bushy area, etc.  That area can be saved for you and others to use in their campaigns.
Campaigns

Once you have areas, you can start building campaigns.  There are two types of campaigns, Story and Challenge.  A story campaign is a linear series of aeras on which you can set parameters such as length, dialogs, etc.  They are usually more story driven and must have an ending.  The other type of campaign is the Challenge campaign which consists of a structured series of area groups (see Groups). Unlike story campaigns, challenge campaigns don't have an ending, they are infinite and have a goal and a goal target, like Kill 500 zombies.

Beyond this simple description is a ton of options you can play with both in story and challenge campaigns.
Groups

While story campaigns have a single hidden area group, challenge campaigns make full use of the groups.  A group contains areas and can be set to randomize those areas or spawn them linearely.  Each group can be set to follow other groups using the Chainable Groups property.  That way you can make sure, for exemple, that a group with forest areas, isn't followed directly by a group with alleyway areas.

Using the chainable groups, you can make linear series of groups, randomized series of groups or all kind of structures you want.  When you click on a group, experiment with the Chainable Groups property, which is a crucial element to challenge campaigns.
Story Endings

In a story campaign, the ending is always on the last area and set on the area's properties.  The ending will be in the last pattern of the area.

For chopper escape and highway transition endings, the highway ramp, exit and rescue chopper will be spawned automatically.
Saving Privately vs. Publicly

When you save a file, you have the option to check the Public checkbox.  When checked, your file will be saved in the public section, available for everyone to see.  For patterns and areas, that means other users will be able to load them and use them in their own campaigns.  For campaigns, it means they'll see it in the User Campaigns section in the main menu.  Only you, however, can load your own campaign in the editor to modify it.  Private files are only seen by you, typically used for work in progress.
Dice Icon

When you see a Dice icon over an object, that means it's a randomized object. Some objects you can place like cars and zombies can be of random types, meaning everytime it loads it will be a different object.  Use them to create variety in your patterns.  You can use the Randomize button to see the effect of random objects.
Base and Additive Values

Base and Additive values are used to create a difficulty progression.  In the campaign properties, you can set the difficulty length, which determines how many patterns you must drive through for the difficulty level to go up.  Using the difficulty level, you can create a progression on different campaign parameters such as the Pattern Ratio, which controls how much of the patterns are actually spawned.  The Base value will be the default starting value and with each difficulty level, it will add the Additive value to the Base value.  So with a Base value of 0.5 and an Additive value of 0.1, the total value will be 0.9 at level 4 (0.5 + (4 x 0.1)).  The campaign always starts at level 0 and each subsequent level will add the additive value to the base value.  Experiment with those parameters to get a better hang of it.
Controls

The Delete key will delete objects, areas and patterns.

The C key will duplicate a selected object in the Pattern mode.
Reordering Areas

You can use the the left arrow and right arrow buttons on the areas at the bottom of the campaign view to reorder your areas.

It's especially useful in story campaigns where you wanna craft your campaign as you wish.
Highway Ramps
You don't need to place highway ramps and exits, they'll be spawned automatically when an non-highway area goes to a highway area and vice versa.
Use your swerve ability (default spacebar) to make sharp turns and dodge obstacles.
Honk your horn (deault F key) to pickup civilians when stopped or ward them away when moving.
Churches are drop points for civilians. They have perks and medications available for purchase with RP.
Police stations are a drop points for civilians. They have perks, weapons, weapon upgrades and ammo for purchase with RP.
Weapon caches have weapons, weapon upgrades, ammo and mounted weapons for your vehicle available for purchase with RP.
By clicking the OPTIONS button in the main menu or in the pause (P) menu, you can adjust controls, volumes and performance.
Make sure your browser isn't set to clear your cache or your save file will be deleted!
Try out user made campaigns and challenges by clicking User Campaigns in the main menu or make your own with the campaign editor!
Enemies that cling to your hood can have their attacks delayed by shooting them or by blowing their arms off.
Swerving (default spacebar) into the side walls in alleyways and highways a couple times can knock off enemies on your hood.
Shooting a fire hydrant appart will create a geyser of water that can extinguish your burning engine.
Individual stats like weapon aiming, weapon handling, weapons reloading, toughness and driving automatically levels up as you play.
Mashing space as the driver and the left mouse button as the gunner will bash a side grappling mutant off!
Mutants will sometimes run in packs of 3 or 4, one of them being an alpha mutant, beware!
Soldier zombies wear armored helmets and vests that randomly block bullets.
Pausing, along with other options can be accessed in-game by moving your mouse near the bottom of the screen.
Ramming your vehicle into an obstacle while a grub zombie is climbing up your bumper will cause it to splatter!
As you encounter new things, important information will added to your survival guide, accessible in the main menu and pause menu.
Road of The Dead 2 auto saves your progress but if your browser clears its cache, you may lose all your save data.
Want a challenge? Try the various challenge modes, accessible from the main menu.
You can gather free ammunition by stopping at abandoned military vehicles scattered throughout the game.
When building your own campaign in the campaign editor, save time by loading and using other users' patterns and areas.
Make sure to click save after you finish making a pattern, area or campaign in the campaign editor.
Make sure you have the latest flash player installed for an optimal playing experience.
If the game is lagging for you, try reducing the quality and turning off Zombie Tints in the options.
Shooting an intact vehicle enough will cause it to explode, causing area damage to everything around it.
Vehicle mounted weapons can't be reloaded, so the weapon itself has to be repurchased to refill its ammo.
Feeding zombies will ignore you unless fired upon.
Timing your reloads and character switches can be the difference between life and death!
Reaching high speeds grants you much higher chance of bashing or gibbing enemies away instead of them grappling onto your hood!
Stopping at garages allows you to repair your vehicle, free of charge and to purchase vehicle upgrades and perks with RP.
Perks can be purchased at some locations and grant you helpful abilities such as lowering RP costs, faster character switches, etc.
You can change all sorts of properties and crazy in-game settings in the campaign editor, accessible from the main menu. Give it a try!
Weapon aiming, handling and reloading will automatically level up as you use each specific weapon.
Diane and Cocheta each have their own weapon loadouts and their personal stat levels. However, perks are shared.
An armless zombie on your hood is much easier to knock off.
The Chopper Support perk is not available in the Lost Guns, Hardcore, Rescue Op and F.U.B.A.R. modes.
Water will not only extinguish a burning engine but will also cool down a smoking one.
When you see a mutant jump toward you, do a hard swerve to move out of his trajectory, otherwise he will land on your hood.
If the campaign editor confuses you, make sure you read the help files to understand the concepts you need to use it.
Firing on soldiers in the F.U.B.A.R. mode will suppress their position and cause them to run to a new firing position.
When you fail, be aware of why you failed and upgrade your arsenal and vehicle accordingly.
In the Rescue Op mode, you can slightly move the helicopter around to give yourself some space or close in on your enemies.
If you have trouble handling the hordes of zombies when you stop at locations, upgrade your Task Speed perk for shorter stops.
Honking at civilians, letting them in your vehile and bringing them to a church or police station will give you RP rewards.
When your vehicle is damaged, drive safely and try to reach a garage for repair.
Shoot mines at the distance to avoid their destructive explosions and the possible chain reactions they can cause.
You might want to give driving and gunning time to both characters to level them up equally.
All types of mine emit beeping sounds so be aware of the surrounding sounds through the chaos.
Blowing up mines, cars and fuel trucks is a good way to get rid of a group of nearby zombies and mutants.
Civilians will not get in your car if you have zombies on your vehicle.  Get rid of them first then honk the civilians again.
You can cycle your weapons with the mouse wheel.  This can be helpful when you need to switch weapon very quickly.
Use any spare time you have to reload your weapons. A fully loaded arsenal can be the difference between life and death.
If the game gradually becomes too laggy despite the low quality settings, try refreshing the browser and therefore the game.
Getting low on ammo? Stop at ammo points or purchase a full ammo replenish at a police station or weapon crate.
When getting ammo, all your weapons, except the one you're currently using, will be reloaded for you as well.
Hurting for resources? The Rescue Op challenge mode can help you earn some RPs if it's unlocked.
Finish the story mode to unlock some of the challenge modes!
Sometimes speed isn't everything. Slowing down in the right areas can make the difference between life and death
If your keys get stuck and you are unable to move, try pressing your direction keys and your swerve/interact key again.
There are no garage or church on the highway. If you need repairs or medicine, stock up before taking the ramp!

init_statics: Damage, as the name implies, affects how much damage each bullet does on your target.
Accuracy affects the bullet spread from firing and the kick back for shotguns. It also affects how fast the bullet spread and kick back recover.
Capacity affects how many rounds/shells your weapon can hold and how many total rounds/shells you can carry for that weapon.
The aiming levels up as you play and affects how responsive your aiming is with the weapon.
The handling levels up as you play and affects your equip/unequip speed, how much kick back you get from hard collisions and how fast you recover from those.
The reloading levels up as you play and affects how fast you reload this weapon. This is crucial when dealing with a crowd of zombies.
The Assault Rifle is a well rounded military issued weapon.  It offers good precision on medium bursts but isn't the most easy to handle weapon.
The Large Machine Gun (LMG) doesn't have good accuracy but makes up for it in fire power and magazine size. Reloading is slow so be careful.
The Compact SMG is a light weight weapon that is easy to handle but doesn't have the best accuracy, it works best with small bursts.
The Assault SMG is a responsive weapon that offers a good balance between aiming speed, handling, damage and mag size.
The pistol offers a great aiming speed but low damage and hard handling on collisions.  However, in dire situations, you can always count on this hand weapon.
The Shotgun is powerful at close range. Be mindful, reloading is slow but can be interrupted. Torso shots have a chance to splatter the zombie.
The auto shotgun delivers quick and powerful shots at short range. Very inaccurate at long range. Torso shots have a chance to splatter the zombie.
